components.name: Stage Plate
components.description: Signature: the 200px box at 1:1 on an 8px/40px blueline grid, with dimension lines measuring the selected layer.
components.css: .ds-stage { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 340px; overflow: hidden; background-color: var(--film); background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(39, 71, 201, 0.15) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(39, 71, 201, 0.15) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(rgba(39, 71, 201, 0.07) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(39, 71, 201, 0.07) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 40px 40px, 40px 40px, 8px 8px, 8px 8px; background-position: center; } .ds-plate { position: relative; width: 200px; height: 200px; } .ds-box { width: 100%; height: 100%; background: #ffffff; box-shadow: 5px 5px 10px 3px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2); } .ds-dims { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: visible; pointer-events: none; } .ds-dims path, .ds-dims rect { fill: none; stroke: var(--blueline); stroke-width: 1; } .ds-outline { stroke-opacity: 0.8; } .ds-reach { stroke-dasharray: 4 3; stroke-opacity: 0.6; } .ds-label { fill: var(--blueline); stroke: var(--film); stroke-width: 3px; paint-order: stroke; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-line { animation: ds-draw 260ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; stroke-dasharray: 400; } @keyframes ds-draw { from { stroke-dashoffset: 400; } to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-line { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Sciagraphy is the drafting art of casting shadows by construction. Layered Shade's interface is that plate: a cool drafting-film ground, graphite ink, hairline rules, and one blue pencil line that carries the shell, the selection, focus, the dimension lines and the copy action. The box in the middle is drawn at 1:1, and when Cotas is on, the selected shadow layer is measured on the plate rather than guessed: its x and y offsets, the outline its spread produces, how far its blur reaches, and the light ray that would cast it.

The tool is dense and quiet because it is used beside a code editor. Three working columns share one screen (controls, plate, code), every value is editable as a number and as a slider, and the code column is a dark graphite sheet that shows character for character what the copy button puts on the clipboard. Depth comes from tone and 1px rules, never from floating panels; the only real shadow on screen is the one the person is building.

The redesign replaced a glassmorphism look with blurred blobs and translucent cards. That look is the anti-reference: the tool's own chrome is opaque, ruled and flat.
keyCharacteristics: Drafting-film neutrals (cool blue-grey) with graphite ink and a single committed blue, blueline.
Red pencil appears only where something is limited or failed.
Overpass for every UI word; Overpass Mono, tabular and ligature-free, for every code character and measured number.
Flat tonal layering: film, raised film, paper, plus a graphite code sheet, divided by 1px hairlines.
Small, consistent corners (4px) and a 4px spacing base.
One signature motion: dimension lines draw in when the selected layer changes.

rules.name: The Blueline Rule
rules.body: Blueline is the committed field: the top bar, selection, focus, the dimension lines and the copy action. Nothing decorative is ever blue.

rules.name: The Red Pencil Rule
rules.body: Red marks a limit or a failure: platform-limit notes, a failed copy, a remove action under the pointer. Never emphasis, never decoration.

rules.name: The Content Owns Color Rule
rules.body: The person's colors live on the plate and in swatches. The chrome stays film, graphite and blueline whatever the person picks.

rules.name: The Measured Figure Rule
rules.body: Any number the person reads as a value (code, px, %, layer specs, dimension labels) is Overpass Mono with tabular figures and ligatures off. Words are Overpass.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy inside the columns comes from weight (400/500/600/700) at 12–14px, not from bigger type. Only the product name reaches 18px.

rules.name: The Copy In View Rule
rules.body: The copy action is pinned at the foot of the code column; on desktop it is always visible without scrolling.

rules.name: The Flat Film Rule
rules.body: Panels never float. If a surface needs separation, change its tone or draw a hairline; the only chrome shadows are the tab lift and the focus halo.

dos: Do keep Blueline (#2747c9) to the shell, selection, focus, the dimension lines and the copy action; everything else is Graphite on film.
Do set every value a person reads as a number in Overpass Mono with tabular figures and ligatures off.
Do separate regions and groups with 1px Hairline rules and spacing (20px between groups), not boxes.
Do state platform limits in place, in red pencil on the code sheet, next to the export they affect and only while they apply.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces: selection and caret in Blueline, `accent-color` Blueline, scrollbar thumbs in Strong Hairline (Sheet Rule on the code sheet).
Do give every control a visible focus: 2px Blueline outline at 2px offset, On Blueline in the top bar, Sheet Blueline on the code sheet, the 3px halo on text fields.
Do keep state transitions at 160ms on the expo ease-out and keep the draw-in as the only authored animation.
Do keep the plate at 1:1 with the grid aligned so the box edges land on 40px lines.
donts: Don't use glass, backdrop blur, blurred blobs or translucent floating panels in the tool's chrome; "Glass" is a preset the person builds, not a style for the interface.
Don't lift panels with drop shadows; depth is tone and hairlines, and the only chrome shadows are the tab lift and the field focus halo.
Don't use red pencil for emphasis, branding or decoration.
Don't add accent colors beyond Blueline and red pencil, or tint the chrome with the person's colors.
Don't round controls past 4px; large radii belong to the person's box.
Don't set headings, labels or prose in Overpass Mono; mono is for code and measurements.
Don't use glyphs or emoji as icons; draw them on the 24px, 1.75-stroke set.
